clauses.reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11006, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11006 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 1789) prints Executive Order 11006 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-02-22; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between Eastern Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving Eastern Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, E.A.L. Chapter; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11006 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

savings.reason: After a bounded search of the full text of EO 12553, the U.S. Code and eCFR (no hits for this order), and the Federal Register catalog notes, no savings clause, exception or surviving legal effect was found; EO 12553 revokes the order without any reservation.
